title: AWS Organizations
description: Learn how AWS Organizations, OUs, SCPs, and IAM Identity Center simplify multi-account management.

data.text: As your organization grows, you may need multiple AWS accounts to separate environments, teams, or workloads. AWS Organizations is a service that lets you centrally manage and govern multiple AWS accounts. It gives you tools to consolidate billing, apply policies, and simplify access across all accounts.

data.title: Why Use Multiple Accounts?
data.text: Separate accounts let you isolate development, testing, and production environments. A billing error or security incident in one account does not affect the others.

Every organization starts with a management account. This is the account you used to create the organization. You can then invite other AWS accounts to join. Within an organization, you can group accounts into Organizational Units (OUs) for easier management.

data.title: Core Concepts
items: Management Account — The primary account that creates the organization and manages settings.
Member Accounts — Accounts that belong to the organization.
Organizational Unit (OU) — A container for accounts that share common requirements. OUs can be nested.
Service Control Policy (SCP) — A policy that restricts which AWS services and actions accounts in an OU can use.

data.text: SCPs define the maximum permissions that accounts in an OU can use. They do not grant permissions directly. Instead, they set guardrails. For example, you could use an SCP to block all accounts in the Production OU from accessing certain services.

data.title: Example Service Control Policy JSON
data.content: This SCP allows all AWS actions but explicitly denies access to the IAM DeleteAccountPolicy API, preventing accounts from deleting critical policies.

data.text: IAM Identity Center is AWS's single sign-on (SSO) solution. It lets users sign in once with their corporate credentials and access all their AWS accounts and applications. This eliminates the need to create and manage separate IAM users in each account.

terms.definition: A service for centrally managing and governing multiple AWS accounts.
The primary AWS account that creates and manages the organization.
A container for grouping accounts that share common permissions or requirements.
A policy that defines the maximum permissions available to accounts in an OU.
AWS's single sign-on service for managing access across multiple AWS accounts and applications.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: AWS Organizations centralizes management of multiple accounts
The management account controls organization-wide settings
OUs group accounts for easier policy management
SCPs set guardrails but do not grant permissions
IAM Identity Center provides single sign-on across all accounts
